title: Claimed AI-Assisted Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced 3D Navier–Stokes Equations
whyItMatters: Claims finite-time blow-up for 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes with zero external force—directly targeting the unforced version experts said OpenAI’s September proof left open.
summary: On the same day as the Riemann Hypothesis release, Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) and Tristan Buckmaster (NYU) posted a 79-page GitHub paper and ~600,000-line Lean 4 library claiming smooth, compactly supported starting data can blow up in finite time for the *unforced* 3D Navier–Stokes equations (disproving Fefferman’s statements A & B). The strategy constructs a discretely self-similar profile numerically and upgrades it via rigorous perturbation theory.
technicalHighlights: Targets the physically core unforced 3D Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize statements (A) and (B) on ℝ³ and the periodic torus.
Accompanied by a 79-page manuscript and ~600,000-line Lean 4 + Mathlib library formalizing the analytical reduction.
Developed using Anthropic’s Claude throughout the analytic derivation and formalization.
caveats: Decisive numerical interval-arithmetic certificate (Arb) has not yet been publicly released (only its hash), and a late Lean patch was not rebuilt; unrefereed claim until the certificate can be independently replayed.

scoreRationale.foundational: If verified, resolves the true unforced 3D Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem open for over a century.
scoreRationale.ripple: Would fundamentally reshape fluid mechanics, turbulence theory, and computer-assisted PDE proofs.
scoreRationale.verification: Scored conservatively (54): Lean formalizes the analytical reduction, but the decisive numerical certificate is not yet public.
scoreRationale.velocity: Moved from forced-equation controversy to an unforced 600K-line Lean + paper claim in just 10 weeks.
